name: VA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+26 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic seats in Virginia
Don Beyer's overwhelming fundraising edge: about $2.5 million raised and $839,000 on hand versus roughly $42,000 for Republican Tony Sabio
Long-serving incumbent seeking re-election with no serious outside spending targeting the seat
Prediction markets price Beyer's win probability near 96%
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: a D+26 district, a well-funded multi-term incumbent, a token Republican operation, and markets pricing the race at near-certain Democratic retention. With no polling or competitive spending to suggest otherwise, a margin in the mid-20s and Safe Democratic status is warranted.
model.watch: Only a dramatic, district-wide collapse in Democratic turnout or an unforeseen scandal would put this seat in any doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 8th District is among the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+26. Don Beyer has held the seat since 2015 and is seeking another term. He has raised roughly $2.5 million with more than $800,000 on hand, while Republican Tony Sabio has raised about $42,000. A Libertarian and an independent candidate are also on the ballot.

No public general-election polling exists for this race, which is typical for districts this lopsided. Prediction markets put Beyer's chances around 96 percent. The district's fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the enormous gap in campaign resources all point to a wide Beyer victory, and the race sits firmly in the Safe Democratic category.
